neighbours.label: the preposition (by / with / to) closing a sentence-initial participle of reaction or confrontation (Shaken by, Faced with, Responding to), against the same prepositions in ordinary non-participial use
fire: The rebels had taken the bridge. Alarmed by the news, the governor sent for troops.
Prices kept rising all winter. Confronted with empty shelves, shoppers turned angry.
The flood reached the town at night. Startled by the sirens, families fled uphill.
Two ships were lost in the storm. Troubled by the losses, the company halted trade.
The strike spread to the docks. Reacting to the pressure, the mayor offered talks.
The enemy fleet appeared at dawn. Surprised by its size, the admiral withdrew.
Sales collapsed in the spring. Faced with ruin, the owners sold the factory.
The verdict was read aloud. Angered by the decision, the crowd began to shout.
quiet: The rebels had taken the bridge. The governor sat by the window and sent for troops.
Prices kept rising all winter. Shoppers came with empty bags and turned angry.
The flood reached the town at night. Families walked to the hills by the old road.
Two ships were lost in the storm. The company halted trade with the eastern ports.
The strike spread to the docks. The mayor went to the harbor and offered talks.
The enemy fleet appeared at dawn. The admiral stood by the mast and withdrew.
Sales collapsed in the spring. The owners sold the factory with its machines.
The verdict was read aloud. The crowd stood by the steps and began to shout.
